question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(8),$ calculate $P(X>0.4).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(8).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}8{e}^{-8x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X>0.4)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>0.4) & ={\int }_{0.4}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0.4}^{\infty }8{e}^{-8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-8x}{|}_{0.4}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-3.2} \\  & ≈0.0408\end{aligned}
$$
